original_value: AbstractSocial media has become a mainstream channel of communication during the COVID‐19 pandemic. While some studies have been developed on investigating public opinion on social media data regarding COVID‐19 pandemic, there is no study analyzing anti‐quarantine comments on social media. This study has collected and analyzed near 80,000 tweets to understand anti‐quarantine social comments. Using text mining, we found 11 topics representing different issues such as comparing COVID‐19 and flu and health side effects of quarantine. We believe that this study shines a light on public opinion of people who are against quarantine.

result.paraphrase: During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media became a mainstream communication channel. Although prior studies have examined public opinion in social media data about COVID-19, no research had analyzed anti-quarantine comments on these platforms. This study gathered and analyzed nearly 80,000 tweets to understand anti-quarantine social commentary. Through text mining, we identified 11 topics covering issues such as comparisons between COVID-19 and flu and the health side effects of quarantine. We believe this study sheds light on the public opinion of people opposed to quarantine.
